method: Recorded at run time, not reconstructed. The AuRUS arm was staged, launched, monitored and closed by the session that authored its harness; this file restates those records. The run window is taken from run.log mtimes in the collected output tree, which the harness writes as each run finishes. The counter arm was added on 2026-08-17/18 through scripts/campaign.py, whose campaign.toml declaration is archived beside this file; it is recorded at run time on the same terms.

profile_commit.subject: fix(experiments): run AuRUS at the pre-fork base, not this project's fork
profile_commit.note: Informational, and deliberately not held by a tag. No counter binary ran in this arm, so this sha pins nothing that determines a result; it names the revision the harness came from, and the harness itself is pinned exactly by the content-addressed blob under vendored_scripts. The 2026-08-17 rebase onto main rewrote this sha (the equivalent post-rebase commit is 87ec8db) and left the vendored blob byte-identical, which is why the rebase costs this record nothing. The version that does determine the results is under `aurus` below, and that one is tagged.

profile_commit_evidence: Both hosts were staged to this commit on branch feat/aurus-h2h before launch, and each host's on-disk scripts/aurus_campaign.py still hashes to the blob this commit records (md5 c35d02c0adf2c5ad43fed052004e2b04, checked 2026-08-17). It is the commit that fixed the corpus at the paper's 26 rows and pointed the harness at the pre-fork AuRUS base.
binary_commit_note: Null for the AuRUS arm by construction rather than by loss: it invokes unreal-repair.sh alone and links no counter binary. The counter arm does have one -- see counter_arm.binary_commit, 1d18cf3 -- so this top-level null describes the AuRUS arm only and must not be read as covering the campaign.

aurus.repo: git@github.com:benmandrew/AuRUS.git (fork of the authors' unreal-repair; also pushed to git@ssh.git.benmandrew.com:me/AuRUS.git)
aurus.note: This is the version that determines every result in this file, and it lives in a different repository, so no tag in the counter repo can hold it. The three fields below are the record: `commit` is the upstream base, `deployed_commit` is the exact tree that ran, and `tracked_file_digest` verifies a deployment without needing either repository.
aurus.subject: minors
aurus.commit_reachable: An ancestor of the branches base, master and spot-ltl, and present on both remotes, so it is held without a tag of its own. It is not a branch tip: master's HEAD is ccb42ea, which carries the fork optimisations this campaign excluded, so checking out master reproduces the wrong thing.
aurus.pin: The campaign is pinned at this commit plus the single documented Strix substitution below. Reproduce by checking out 3f6f01f and replacing lib/new_strix/strix with a Linux build of Strix 21.0.0.

tracked_file_digest.over: the 6713 tracked files of 3f6f01f, with the Strix substitution applied
tracked_file_digest.recipe: git ls-files | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs sha256sum | sha256sum
tracked_file_digest.verified: 2026-08-17: identical on the local worktree, av2 and av3. A whole-directory digest deliberately is not used, because `ant compile` writes bin/ class files that differ per host and are not part of what ran.
tracked_file_digest.purpose: Checks a deployment against what ran using nothing but the files on disk, so the archive stays verifiable if the AuRUS repository becomes unavailable.

aurus.deployment: rsynced to both hosts at ~/projects/tools/aurus-base without .git, so the hosts carry the tree and not the history.

deviations.reason: The blob 3f6f01f tracks is a macOS Mach-O executable. On Linux it does not run, realizability checking fails, and every run returns zero solutions. This is the only file that differs from the base tree, and the substitution is unavoidable on this hardware.
deviations.same_version: Both blobs are Strix 21.0.0. The deployed one answers `--version` with `strix 21.0.0`; the macOS blob carries the same version string and the same CLI strings. The swap is a platform build, so it changes no behaviour of the realizability check.
deviations.blob_origin: The deployed blob was introduced by fork commit 6546a6c (`Split semantic factor into strengthening and weakening`), which is a descendant of 3f6f01f rather than upstream, and is the blob the fork still tracks at ccb42ea. So the bytes come from the fork's history even though the version matches upstream's. Nothing else from that commit is present.
deviations.verified: file(1) reports ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable on both hosts; no run.log contains an ERR: lib/new_strix/strix line.

aurus.not_deviations: Deliberately absent: the fork's SPOT satisfiability swap, its solver cache, and its parallel ranking. The arm runs the authors' algorithm as they left it.

flags.factors_note: Settings.setFactors halves the semantic weight into LOST_MODELS_FACTOR and WON_MODELS_FACTOR, so -factors=0.7,0.1,0.2 is the 0.7/0.1/0.1/0.1 weighting requested. It is also the shipped default and what two of the three upstream drivers use.
flags.only_inputs_a_basis: The nine families the upstream drivers pass -onlyInputsA for; no per-group -factors override was applied, at the user's direction.
flags.no_reference_flags: No -ref flags. Scoring is against this project's examples/<spec>/fixes through the compare binary, so both arms are one statistic over two populations. AuRUS's own case-studies/*/genuine/ directories are never read.

run_window.note: From run.log mtimes across the collected tree. av3's clock runs about 17 minutes fast, so its half carries that skew. Wall time per host as the harness reported it: av2 1422.4 min, av3 1455.5 min.

corpus.description: The 26 TLSF specifications of the AuRUS paper, at the paths named in SPEC_TLSF. Six carry an -aurus suffix because this project has same-named families at different SYNTCOMP parameter instances. lily02 points at case-studies/syntcomp-unreal/lily02/lilydemo02.tlsf, the paper's row, whose file is byte-identical to the top-level copy.
corpus.counter_scope: The counter arm ran 25 of the 26. humanoid-741 is held out permanently as unscoreable -- its own input is ill-separated, well-separation reads the assumption side alone, and the only assumption-side operator move strengthens the conjunction, so no descendant can repair it. AuRUS also returned nothing for it across all 30 repeats. Recorded in H2H_UNSCOREABLE and enforced by test_experiment_paths.py.

results.integrity: The n_solutions column sums to 287006 and the collected tree holds exactly 287006 spec*.tlsf files. All 780 rows have a run.log.

well_separation_sweep.scope: full: every one of the 287,006 candidate repairs, not a sample
well_separation_sweep.tool: scripts/check_well_separated.py, which re-derives the query from the TLSF text and calls ltlsynt directly. Deliberately not counter's in-run checker, which maps a realizability timeout to unrealizable and caches it -- for this query that reads as well-separated, so a verdict taken from it would launder timeouts into passes.
well_separation_sweep.fast_path: off, so every verdict came from ltlsynt. Exactly 2 ill-separated files had input-only assumptions and would have been misclassified as well-separated by the fast path.
well_separation_sweep.cost: 1.99 core-hours; mean 0.025s per ltlsynt call, max 0.25s against a 60s timeout that was never approached.
well_separation_sweep.meaning: AuRUS ran with -addA and may add assumptions freely, so a repair can reach realizability by adding assumptions the system then defeats. Two in five of its claimed repairs do exactly that. Any comparison quoting AuRUS's repair count without this correction overstates the baseline by that margin.
well_separation_sweep.distribution: Bimodal rather than uniform, so the per-family split matters more than the mean: lily16 98.1% and load-balancer-aurus 91.4% at one end; rg2, arbiter-aurus and humanoid-458 at 0.0% and rg1 at one file out of 7442 at the other.
well_separation_sweep.families_with_no_output: Five of the 26 emitted no repairs at all across 30 repeats each -- full-arbiter-aurus, humanoid-503, humanoid-531, humanoid-741, prioritized-arbiter-aurus -- so they contribute no denominator. They are exactly the five that capped 30/30 in the results CSV, two independent measurements agreeing.
well_separation_sweep.denominator_caveat: Measured over every emitted file rather than only those counter's `realize` confirms realizable. AuRUS emits only what Strix accepts, so the two should be close, but the exact figure waits on the aurus_validate run, which produces both columns in one pass.
well_separation_sweep.csvs: experiments/aurus-h2h/wellsep-av2.csv and wellsep-av3.csv, gitignored with the rest of the results. The sweep ran on each host over the half already on its disk; the two row counts sum to 287006 exactly.
well_separation_sweep.csv_note: The sweep tool's arm/spec columns are empty here: parse_run_id expects run_experiments' `sweep_..._seedNN` directory layout and the AuRUS tree is <family>/repeat-NN/, so family attribution comes from the path column.

caveats: The counter arm has not run. This directory records one side of a head-to-head, and no comparison may be drawn from it alone.

AuRUS is not seedable: Settings.RANDOM_GENERATOR draws from Math.random(). The mitigation is 30 repeats per family with every run's log and solution set archived, the same mitigation the 2026-07-24 campaign used.

Two full-arbiter-aurus runs (av2 repeat-04, av3 repeat-20) exited 137 with an empty n_solutions and no killed flag. The JVM was SIGKILLed under -Xmx8g while the harness timeout had not fired, which is the kernel OOM killer rather than a cap. They are failures and belong in neither the completed nor the capped bucket.

Cap rate concentrates in six families. humanoid-503, humanoid-531 and humanoid-741 capped 30 of 30; full-arbiter-aurus produced nothing at all (28 capped plus the 2 OOM rows); prioritized-arbiter-aurus capped 29 of 30 and pcar-v2-888 25 of 30. lily02 capped once. The other 20 families capped zero times.
Completing runs finish far below the budget: median wall 150 s against a 7200 s cap, maximum 6508 s. The capped runs are hard rather than marginal, so a longer budget would not convert many of them.
The macOS Strix substitution above is a deviation from the base tree and is not optional on Linux.

The counter arm will run against different engine code than the branch carried while the AuRUS arm ran. The 2026-08-17 rebase brought in ten commits, three of which change behaviour: selection_scheme now defaults to nsga2-apportion (c71ecf0), the MRS walk defaults to conflict-degree admission order (aa050f6), and crossover grafts donors from anywhere in the parent (5f2ae7b). None of this touches the AuRUS arm, which links no counter binary, so the results above are unaffected. The counter arm's own binary_commit records what it actually ran.

campaign.toml declares the seed split for the counter phase only. The AuRUS repeats were split by aurus_campaign.py --repeat-offset instead, which is why the host ranges here read 0-14 and 15-29 rather than the 0-9 and 10-19 that file names.

Unresolved compare verdicts. `compare` returned `unknown` on 36 of the 780 AuRUS repeats, meaning it hit the 300s per-call timeout rather than deciding, and those read as zero in the rate. They fall in two families: humanoid-742, all 30 repeats, whose AuRUS rate of 0/30 is therefore unmeasured rather than measured-zero; and lift, 6 of 30. AuRUS claimed 600-690 repairs per repeat on humanoid-742 against a 5.8K ideal, which is what blew the timeout. The bias runs against AuRUS, so resolving it can only widen a lead that is already significant: humanoid-742 is currently a tie contributing nothing to the test, and lift already favours AuRUS. Both families were re-run at a 3600s timeout on 2026-08-18 -- see recheck below.

The July comparison is not carried forward and must not be cited beside these numbers as though the two were commensurable. Its AuRUS arm was misconfigured (see decision_mechanism), its counter arm ran at a 600s cap against 7200s here, the ideal set has changed for at least three families, and PLAN §7.5 and §10.3 list seven intervening engine changes.

vendored_scripts.note: Verbatim copies of the drivers that ran both arms, so the directory reproduces without the git history. aurus_campaign.py ran the AuRUS arm; campaign.py, gen_configs.py, run_experiments.py and merge_experiments.py ran and collected the counter arm; aurus_validate.py and check_well_separated.py produced the AuRUS quality and well-separation columns. analyse_aurus_h2h.py, which computes the decision, lives in scripts/ rather than here because it ran nothing. maximal.cpp and maximality_sweep.py produced the diversity comparison, and maximal.cpp is the first vendored file that is not a script: reproducing that measurement is a compile rather than an invocation, so the source is what has to be held. It needs the rest of the tree at its source_commit to build, which the vendored copy alone does not supply -- the copy pins what was compiled, and the commit is where the build comes from.

configs.source: Pulled from av2 rather than from the analyst's checkout. The local experiments/configs-aurus-h2h held nsga2-truncate, stale from before the profile followed the selection default to nsga2-apportion, while the hosts held what ran.

decision.rule: PLAN.md §5, as amended by §10.1 (the primary rate is over well-separated repairs only) and §10.2 (the test is run over families and over clusters, and the clustered result governs where the two disagree).
decision.agreement: Both tests reject at alpha 0.05 in the same direction, so §10.2's tie-breaker is not needed.
decision.test_note: The p-values are exact, built by enumerating sign assignments of the observed ranks rather than read from a table. Rates of k/20 against k/30 tie constantly, and averaged ties make the ranks fractional, where a table built on distinct integer ranks no longer applies.
decision.statement: On this corpus at this operating point, AuRUS scores higher on the pre-registered repair-quality endpoint. Reported as measured, with no re-run and no post-hoc arm added to recover it, as §5 outcome 2 requires.

decision_mechanism.purpose: Why the result came out this way. None of this changes the outcome above, which stands as the pre-registered rule computes it. It is recorded because the outcome inverts the July 2026 comparison, and the reason is checkable.

1_counter_did_not_regress.claim: counter's side is flat against July. Nine of the ten families shared with the 2026-07-24 ablation moved by at most 0.15.
1_counter_did_not_regress.wider_check: Across every archived campaign that ran these families -- up to eleven campaigns and several thousand rows per family -- this campaign's implies_ideal sits at or above the historical range, and found_repair sits at the top of it. rg1 found a repair in 100% of runs here against 43.8-79.6% historically, humanoid-531 in 100% against 64.4-98.8%.
1_counter_did_not_regress.standing_zeros: The families reading 0% are not new failures. gyro-var1 and lift are 0% implies_ideal across eleven campaigns; gyro-var2, humanoid-458 and rg1 across every campaign that ran them. counter finds repairs on all of them at 99-100% yield, and those repairs have never implied an ideal.

2_the_one_real_move_is_a_scoring_target_.cause: Its ideal set went from four files to two between the campaigns: d4ba384 dropped arbiter_fixed3, 2e3969d dropped arbiter_fixed0 and arbiter_fixed2, and 3833dd9 added weaken-grant-exclusion. Dropping targets can only lower implies_ideal. PLAN §7.2 records this family as now resting partly on a hand-derived weakening rather than on verbatim AuRUS repairs.

3_what_actually_flipped_is_the_aurus_arm.claim: July ran AuRUS misconfigured, and this campaign is the corrected re-run its own audit asked for.
3_what_actually_flipped_is_the_aurus_arm.july_misconfiguration: experiments/2026-07-24-ablation/REPORT.md found that arm used -k=10 against the paper's -k=20, halving the model-counting bound its semantic-similarity fitness rests on, and -GATO=3600 against the published 7200. That report withheld confidence in July's 0.300-against-0.192 quality result and asked for a corrected re-run before the gap was treated as sound.
3_what_actually_flipped_is_the_aurus_arm.reading: Correcting the configuration turned four zeros into near-ones. July's 'counter beats AuRUS on quality' was measured against a crippled baseline, which the project had already said in writing.

4_the_endpoint_rewards_candidate_volume.claim: The endpoint asks whether any returned repair implies an ideal, and the two tools return very different numbers of candidates.

per_candidate_hit_rate.note: counter is 2.8x more precise per repair it returns, and more precise on 13 of the 25 families; AuRUS is more precise on 7 and both are zero on 5. counter offers about 60x fewer draws at the target because step 6 of its pipeline keeps only the maximal specifications while AuRUS returns everything it found.

exploratory.status: NOT pre-registered. These qualify the reading of the outcome; they do not replace it, and §5 forbids a post-hoc arm added to recover a result.
exploratory.counterfactual_method: 1 - (1 - p_counter)^k_aurus per family, p_counter being counter's per-candidate hit rate and k_aurus AuRUS's candidates per repeat. It assumes candidates are independent, which they are not -- counter's come from one converged population -- so it brackets the effect as an upper bound rather than measuring it.

counter_arm_secondary.solutions_per_run: counter median 4 maximal repairs against AuRUS median 424 claimed, 240 after the §10.1 filter. The two counts mean different things and are recorded rather than compared, per §6.
counter_arm_secondary.aurus_revalidation: 286200 of 287006 claimed repairs REALIZABLE under ltlsynt, 806 disagreements.
counter_arm_secondary.reconciliation_with_the_standalone_sweep: The standalone sweep recorded 113958 ill-separated of 287006 (39.71%); aurus_validate.py records 113283 (39.47%). The sweep asked every emitted file, while validation asks only the repairs `realize` confirms REALIZABLE -- there is no strategy to defeat the assumptions with otherwise. The 675 difference sits inside the 806 repairs the two tools disagree on, so the counts are consistent rather than in conflict.
counter_arm_secondary.well_separation_filter_effect: The §10.1 filter moved exactly 2 of 25 family rates: lift 0.167 -> 0.300 and lily11 0.900 -> 0.833. The unfiltered per-family test, which is what §5 originally named, gives p = 0.0140 in the same direction.

arms.note: Two arms, recorded in one file. The unqualified top-level blocks -- run_window, hosts, corpus, results, well_separation_sweep, flags, aurus -- describe the AuRUS arm, which ran first and was archived before the counter arm existed. counter's are under counter_arm and counter_arm_secondary. The comparison of the two is under decision and decision_mechanism.

recheck.scope: humanoid-742 (30 repeats) and lift (30 repeats), both hosts
recheck.reason: The first validation pass ran compare at a 300s per-call timeout and returned `unknown` on 36 of 780 repeats, which read as zero in the rate. This pass re-asks them at 3600s.
recheck.cannot_change_the_outcome: Resolving an unknown can only add AuRUS successes, never remove one. humanoid-742 is currently a tie contributing nothing to the test, and lift already favours AuRUS, so the direction of the decision is fixed either way and only the margin can move. The decision block is therefore final as recorded; this block takes the resolved counts when the pass lands.
recheck.command: scripts/aurus_validate.py --aurus-out ~/h2h-recheck --jobs 8 --timeout 3600, over a symlink tree of the two families

diversity.status: complete as of 2026-08-19, with one gap. humanoid-742 carries no diversity number in either arm: 30 of its 30 AuRUS repeats hit the wall cap, and its one measured counter directory capped at 900 s under the shorter cap the 2026-08-18 attempt used. The 2026-08-19 sweep excluded the family rather than re-running it, so the gap is a decision not to spend the time and not an unfinished measurement.
diversity.question: Whether AuRUS's candidate-count advantage over counter -- 317 against 4 per run, the volume asymmetry recorded in decision_mechanism part 4 -- survives being asked as a question about distinct repairs rather than about files. Every one of AuRUS's 287,006 outputs is syntactically distinct, verbatim and comment-stripped, so nothing cheaper than an implication sweep can answer it.
diversity.method: Both arms through counter's own TLSF maximality filter, tlsf_make_implication_filter, exposed over a directory by the maximal binary. Two counts per directory: `maximal`, the specs no other spec strictly dominates, which is the filter counter runs and keeps whole equivalence classes together; and `classes`, those survivors quotiented by mutual implication.
diversity.why_two_counts: AuRUS's own MaximalSolutions filter is not the same predicate and would not give the same number. It marks `to` subsumed on any `from => to`, without requiring the converse to fail, and its already-subsumed skip then spares the rest of the class -- so each equivalence class collapses to one survivor whose identity depends on execution order. That is `classes`, reported under a name that reads like `maximal`. Both counts are recorded here so the comparison does not turn on which definition was used. The underlying implication check agrees between the two tools: flat whole-formula LTL, `f1 & !(f2)` unsat, no assume-guarantee contravariance.
diversity.results: AuRUS arm: 596 directory measurements, 566 complete and 30 at the per-directory wall cap, all 30 of them humanoid-742, 15 per host. Medians per repeat are 480 distinct, 45 maximal and 40 classes, over totals of 268,138 distinct, 28,689 maximal and 25,011 classes. The filter removes 89.3% of AuRUS's output, and quotienting the survivors removes a further 12.8%. counter arm: 447 run directories, 446 complete and 1 capped, that one being humanoid-742 seed 16, over 25 families and 20 seeds, so the arm is covered in full apart from that directory. Medians per run are 4 distinct, 4 maximal and 3 classes, over totals of 2,251 files, 2,176 distinct, 2,160 maximal and 1,502 classes. The filter removes 0.7% and quotienting removes a further 30.5%, so of 2,160 maximal specifications only 1,502 are distinct strongest repairs. The raw candidate advantage recorded in decision_mechanism part 4 was AuRUS 317 against counter 4; measured as maximal specifications it is 45 against 4, and as equivalence classes 40 against 3. The asymmetry drops by roughly an order of magnitude and survives.
diversity.control: counter's arm goes through the same filter, which is also the idempotence check: its pipeline already applied it at step 6, so `maximal` should equal `distinct` on every counter row. It does not hold universally. 10 of the 446 rows have `maximal` below `distinct` and lose 16 specifications between them, in pcar-v2-888 on 7 of its 19 runs, and in full-arbiter-aurus, prioritized-arbiter-aurus and humanoid-531 on one run each. The cause is established, and it is a budget mismatch rather than a defect in the filter. The campaign config sets black_timeout_ms = 1000 while both `maximal` and `compare` hardcode a 20,000 ms black budget, and `check_pair` in src/tlsf/filter.cpp reads both directions through `.value_or(false)`, so an inconclusive check counts as no implication and neither specification is marked subsumed. Any implication query taking between 1 s and 20 s therefore decides under `maximal` and times out during the run, leaving the dominated specification in the output. src/filter/implication.cpp:40 does the same on the FRETISH path. counter's reported repair counts are a superset of the maximal antichain wherever the 1 s budget bites.
diversity.counts_are_upper_bounds: Both reported counts are upper bounds, because the binary resolves an undecided solver call the way the engine does. `check_pair` reads each direction through `.value_or(false)`, so a timed-out implication leaves neither specification subsumed and both stay in `maximal`. The class quotient at src/maximal.cpp:221-224 applies the same convention to both directions of the equivalence test, so a timed-out pair is counted as two classes rather than one. This is the `.value_or(false)` convention the control block describes at the 1 s budget, operating here at 20 s, so it is a smaller effect and not a different one. `maximal` reports no undecided count, so neither bound can be tightened from the data already collected. The direction is fixed: both counts can only be too high, never too low, so the measured 89.3% collapse of AuRUS's output is a lower bound on the true collapse, and the arm comparison is conservative in AuRUS's favour rather than counter's.
diversity.cost: Not the quadratic the pair enumeration suggests. check_pair short-circuits once either endpoint is flagged, so a subsumed spec stops paying for its remaining pairs and the cost lands near n times the surviving set. Measured 86 CPU-seconds for 275 candidates, against the ~35 CPU-minutes 37,675 pairs at the measured 28 ms per implication check would have cost.
diversity.hosts: av2 and av3 each swept their own AuRUS output at --jobs 6, under an 1800 s per-directory wall cap. The counter arm was first attempted on 2026-08-18 in a local worktree at --jobs 8, which exhausted the 30 GB desktop and triggered a global out-of-memory kill at 18:24: three ltlfilt children held 9.6 GB, 4.8 GB and 4.5 GB, and the kernel killed a process inside the terminal's cgroup, taking the sweep down with it. `maximal` raises ltlfilt_timeout to 300,000 ms against the 10,000 ms default, which is part of how a blowing-up ltlfilt got that far. The run's 218 completed rows were recovered from the dead session's scratchpad. The arm was then swept on av2 and av3 on 2026-08-19 at --jobs 8 under the same 1800 s cap, with humanoid-742 excluded. The three runs overlap on 287 keys and agree on every count, so the measurement is deterministic and the salvaged rows are sound. A capped directory is recorded as such rather than dropped, so the sweep never reports a diversity number it did not finish measuring. Sweeps belong on the lab hosts, at 125 GB and 32 cores each, and not on the 30 GB desktop.
diversity.cannot_change_the_outcome: Scoring is existential: a run scores 1 when at least one of its repairs is equivalent to or strictly stronger than at least one ideal. `compare` decides that with `tlsf_spec_implies` on the TLSF path, the same predicate `maximal` applies, at the same 20 s budget. Every element of a finite set sits below some maximal element under that order, and implication is transitive, so if any repair implies an ideal then some maximal repair does too. Filtering to the maximal set therefore leaves implies_ideal and implies_genuine exactly where they were. The 10 timeout exceptions recorded under control cannot move either rate, since the extra specifications are dominated ones whose dominators are retained and score at least as well. Diversity is a separate axis and is reported as one. The decision still stands on implies_ideal and implies_genuine.
